question.text: Loss aversion in the context of retirement planning leads to:

answer.text: Excessive risk-taking to recover past losses
Fear-driven inaction or under-investment in growth assets, resulting in insufficient retirement corpus
Over-diversification across too many asset classes

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XVII (p.91), fear of losses can cause investors to be inactive or to under-invest in growth assets, which can leave the retirement corpus inadequate. The Trap: Loss aversion does not generally drive excessive risk-taking — that pattern is associated with other biases. Loss aversion typically results in over-caution, not over-diversification or perfectly rational decisions. Note: Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) can help loss-averse clients build equity exposure gradually and reduce the emotional impact of short-term volatility.
